description: HyGLEAM is a *memetic algorithm*: an evolutionary algorithm that also improves some children by a local search. Here the evolutionary part is GLEAM's diffusion model, and the local searchers are random-mutation hill climbing or, for real parameters, Rosenbrock's rotating-coordinates method. The best setting is problem-dependent, so HyGLEAM adapts two choices while it runs: how often a child is improved (the *frequency*) and how many evaluations one local search may use (the *intensity*). Each choice is a small set of levels with probabilities, and the levels that gave the largest relative cost gain per evaluation get more probability. A *Lamarckian* run writes the improved genome back; a *Baldwinian* run keeps only its improved cost. Use it when local search pays off but its right amount is unknown; it is a heuristic with no optimality guarantee.

papers.authors: Wilfried Jakob, Christian Blume, Georg Bretthauer
papers.title: Towards a Generally Applicable Self-Adapting Hybridization of Evolutionary Algorithms
